rows.verbatim: Drop pipe shall be 1.5” diameter, Galvanized steel, Schedule 40, pipe shall be in accordance with ASTM A53 Grade B and have threaded and coupled fittings in accordance with ANSI B16.1.

rows.verbatim: Pipe shall be NSF 61 approved and rated not less than 200 psig.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide pipe that is NSF 61 approved and rated no less than 200 psig.

rows.verbatim: Check valves shall be of the same size as the drop pipe and placed every 200’ with one being just above the pump.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall install check valves the same size as the drop pipe, placed every 200 feet with one just above the pump.

rows.verbatim: Check valve body shall be lead-free bronze or brass, with stainless steel spring material and be NSF-61 approved.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide check valve bodies of lead-free bronze or brass with stainless steel spring material, NSF-61 approved.

rows.verbatim: Valves must be rated to at least 200 psi water pressure and designed for either horizontal or vertical orientation.
rows.normalized: Contractor's valves must be rated to at least 200 psi and designed for horizontal or vertical orientation.

rows.verbatim: Valve body must be rated to handle the weight of the pump and drop pipe assembly, water column and pressure.
rows.normalized: Contractor's valve body must be rated to handle the weight of the pump/drop pipe assembly, water column, and pressure.

rows.verbatim: Torque Arrestors shall be flexible molded rubber adjustable torque arrestors that adjusts to fit 4” to 8” diameter well casings, placed at each check valve location.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide flexible molded rubber adjustable torque arrestors fitting 4-8 inch diameter well casings, placed at each check valve location.

rows.verbatim: Each torque arrestor shall include 2 each stainless-steel hose clamps to secure the torque arrestor to the drop pipe.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall include 2 stainless-steel hose clamps per torque arrestor to secure it to the drop pipe.

rows.verbatim: Well cap shall meet State of Missouri requirements but must be at least a metal sanitary cap that fits over the top of the casing forming a waterproof and vermin seal with threaded hole for electrical PVC conduit.
rows.normalized: Contractor's well cap shall meet Missouri requirements and must be at least a metal sanitary cap forming a waterproof, vermin-proof seal with a threaded hole for electrical PVC conduit.

rows.verbatim: Well cap shall have an integral vent screen.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a well cap with an integral vent screen.

rows.verbatim: The vent shall terminate in a downturned position, at or above the top of the casing or pitless unit in a minimum 1 ½ inch
rows.normalized: Contractor shall terminate the vent in a downturned position at or above the top of the casing or pitless unit (minimum 1 1/2 inch, detail continues on next page).

rows.verbatim: The pipe connecting the casing to the vent shall be of adequate size to provide rapid venting of the casing.
rows.normalized: Contractor must size the vent-connecting pipe adequately to provide rapid venting of the casing.

rows.verbatim: There shall be no other openings in the well cap.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure the well cap has no openings other than those specified.

rows.verbatim: The well cap shall be lockable, Baker-Monitor well cap part number 6WTCL or approved equal.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a lockable well cap, Baker-Monitor part number 6WTCL or approved equal.

rows.verbatim:
G. Pitless adapter shall be a weld on type or approved equal, State of Missouri approved, with
minimum 3.5’ bury depth.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a weld-on type pitless adapter (or approved equal), State of Missouri approved, with minimum 3.5' bury depth.

rows.verbatim: B. Pipe thread compound shall be Blue Magic Industrial Grade or approved equal.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use Blue Magic Industrial Grade pipe thread compound or approved equal.

rows.verbatim:
It shall be NDF 61 approved for potable water, grit free, lead free and non-hardening once applied to the pipe
threads.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use pipe thread compound that is NDF 61 approved for potable water, grit free, lead free, and non-hardening once applied.

rows.verbatim:
Samples of water shall be collected in laboratory provided sample
bottles and tested by a State of Missouri certified laboratory for the following constituents:
rows.normalized: Contractor shall collect water samples in laboratory-provided bottles and have them tested by a State of Missouri certified laboratory for listed constituents.

rows.verbatim: The contractor shall coordinate with the Public Utility (PU) provider, Ameren, to pay all fees and provide all labor, materials and equipment to extend their primary distribution system which includes transformers, meter bases, metering, and service connection requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall coordinate with Ameren to pay all fees and provide labor, materials, and equipment to extend the primary distribution system.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide the COR with copies of all permit applications and other requirements provided by the utility company for review.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide the COR with copies of all permit applications and utility company requirements for review.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide and install the electrical system as shown on the drawings and indicated in the specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide and install the electrical system as shown on drawings and specifications.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor is required to provide all additional equipment, materials, and labor necessary to complete the electrical system and make it fully operational in accordance with the Contract and National Electric Code (NFPA 70) latest edition.
rows.normalized: Contractor is required to provide additional equipment, materials, and labor to complete and make the electrical system fully operational per NEC latest edition.

rows.verbatim: Transformer, meter/panel locations, and feeder corridors shall be staked in the field and reviewed and approved by the COR prior to the start of any electrical work.
rows.normalized: Transformer, meter/panel locations, and feeder corridors shall be staked in the field and reviewed/approved by the COR before electrical work begins.

rows.verbatim: All materials shall conform to the applicable current standards (standard rules, regulations and specifications), Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE), Insulated Power Cable Engineers Association (IPCEA), NFPA-70 National Electric Code (NEC).
rows.normalized: Contractor's materials shall conform to applicable IEEE/IPCEA/NFPA-70 NEC standards and regulations.

rows.verbatim: All materials shall bear the label of, or be listed by, the Underwriter’s Laboratory, Inc., (U.L.).
rows.normalized: Contractor's materials shall bear the U.L. label or be U.L.-listed.

rows.verbatim: Where conflicts exist between any of the above standards, the standard which is the most stringent shall take precedence.
rows.normalized: When standards conflict, the contractor shall apply the most stringent standard.

rows.verbatim: Any errors found in the plans or specifications shall be brought to the attention of the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall bring any errors found in plans or specifications to the COR's attention.

rows.verbatim: Contractor is responsible for execution of all work to meet applicable codes.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for executing all work to meet applicable codes.

rows.verbatim: All work shall be done by electricians licensed by the State of Missouri.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall have all work performed by electricians licensed by the State of Missouri.

rows.verbatim: All penetrations through fire rated walls and floors shall be fire sealed with UL listed fire rated material.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall fire seal all penetrations through fire rated walls and floors with UL listed fire rated material.

rows.verbatim: All exposed conduit shall be clean and in new condition free of dents and machine markings.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall keep all exposed conduit clean and in new condition, free of dents and machine markings.

rows.verbatim: Equipment or panels that are being replaced shall have wire numbers put on each conductor prior to removing equipment and a drawing of the connections be made for reconnection of the conductors.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall put wire numbers on each conductor of equipment/panels being replaced prior to removal, and make a drawing of connections for reconnection.

rows.verbatim: Wire numbers shall correspond to control panel schematic and wiring diagram's external connection terminal numbers.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure wire numbers correspond to the control panel schematic and wiring diagram's external connection terminal numbers.

rows.verbatim: Contractor shall provide motor disconnects, where specified, shown or required by code, under this division of the specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide motor disconnects where specified, shown, or required by code.

rows.verbatim: those below grade shall be made by a fusion-welding process.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make grounding connections below grade by a fusion-welding process.

rows.verbatim: Where not otherwise indicated, grounding conductor size shall conform to the most stringent of the governing codes.
rows.normalized: Contractor must size grounding conductors to conform to the most stringent governing code where not otherwise indicated.

rows.verbatim: A ground rod enclosure shall be provided flush at final grade with a lid to access ground connection.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a ground rod enclosure flush at final grade with an access lid for the ground connection.

rows.verbatim: The instrument must be equipped with a meter reading directly in ohms or fractions thereof to indicate the ground value of the ground rod or grounding systems under test.
rows.normalized: The ground resistance tester instrument must be equipped with a meter reading directly in ohms (or fractions) to indicate the ground value of the ground rod or grounding system under test.

rows.verbatim: Measured resistance from rod to earth shall be 25 ohms or less and less then 15 ohms for a ground ring measure at point of connection.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure measured resistance from rod to earth is 25 ohms or less, and less than 15 ohms for a ground ring measured at the point of connection.

rows.verbatim: Minimum resistance shall be 200 megohms.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure minimum insulation resistance is 200 megohms.

rows.verbatim: All electronic devices must be disconnected to avoid damage.
rows.normalized: Contractor must disconnect all electronic devices during insulation resistance testing to avoid damage.

rows.verbatim: GFI breakers in branch panels must be removed, with the phase and neutral wires connected to an adjacent breaker for testing.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove GFI breakers in branch panels and connect phase and neutral wires to an adjacent breaker for testing.

rows.verbatim: The neutral and isolated ground must be disconnected from ground at the main service switchgear in order to test the feeders.
rows.normalized: Contractor must disconnect the neutral and isolated ground from ground at the main service switchgear to test the feeders.

rows.verbatim: Failure of any phase of the operation tests shall constitute failure of the system.
rows.normalized: Contractor's system testing is considered failed if any phase of the operation tests fails.

rows.verbatim: Shop drawings shall include, an overall system drawing, one-line fault current diagram with system fault calculations and Short Circuit Current Requirements (SCCR) determine and shown for all panelboards, disconnects and other equipment where a SCCR is required.
rows.normalized: Contractor's shop drawings must include an overall system drawing, one-line fault current diagram with fault calculations, and SCCR shown for all panelboards, disconnects, and equipment requiring SCCR.

rows.verbatim: Calculations shall be performed after coordination with the electric utility provider to determine the supply side transformer sizes and impedance.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform calculations after coordinating with the electric utility provider to determine supply side transformer sizes and impedance.

rows.verbatim: For bidding purchases the contractor shall base cost on requirements shown in the drawings.
rows.normalized: For bidding purposes, the contractor must base cost on requirements shown in the drawings.

rows.verbatim: Panelboard drawings shall provide detail of the size, materials, and ratings of all panel board construction components including circuit breakers.
rows.normalized: Contractor's panelboard drawings must detail the size, materials, and ratings of all panelboard construction components, including circuit breakers.

rows.verbatim: A listing of compliance standards shall be provided.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a listing of compliance standards.

rows.verbatim:
Receptacle nameplates shall have panel and circuit number engraved at top of plate in 0.25 inch
high letters.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall engrave receptacle nameplates with panel and circuit number at top of plate in 0.25 inch high letters.

rows.verbatim:
Engraving shall be filled with black enamel for ivory plates, white enamel for brown
plates and ivory plates filled with orange paint for isolated ground receptacle.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall fill engraving with black enamel (ivory plates), white enamel (brown plates), or orange paint (isolated ground receptacle, ivory plates).

rows.verbatim: Compression fittings shall be applied with a factory matched die in a hydraulic compression tool that stamps manufacturers name when fully compressed to manufactures specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall apply compression fittings using a factory matched die in a hydraulic compression tool that stamps manufacturer's name when fully compressed to manufacturer's specifications.

rows.verbatim: All feeder terminations shall be rated at 75 degrees C. or higher.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure all feeder terminations are rated at 75 degrees C or higher.

rows.verbatim: Excessive bending of the cable will not be permitted.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not excessively bend the cable during handling.

rows.verbatim:
Non-metallic conduit and fitting shall be electrical grade, UL Listed, schedule 40 PVC and shall
conform to applicable sections of NEMA TC2-latest edition and UL 651.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use electrical grade, UL Listed, schedule 40 PVC non-metallic conduit and fittings conforming to NEMA TC2 and UL 651.

rows.verbatim: Any PVC conduit not having the proper NEMA and UL markings will not be accepted.
rows.normalized: PVC conduit lacking proper NEMA and UL markings will be rejected by the government.

rows.verbatim: Only gray-colored conduit will be accepted.
rows.normalized: Contractor must supply only gray-colored conduit.

rows.verbatim:
Coilable Duct for directional boring installations shall be high density polyethylene (HDPE) in
3”, 4”, or 5” nominal inside diameter, as specified on the Drawings and shall meet ASTM D-
1248.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use HDPE coilable duct (3, 4, or 5 inch nominal ID) meeting ASTM D-1248 for directional boring installations.

rows.verbatim: The stripes shall have a thickness in range of 10-15 mils and be 3/16’ to 3/8” wide.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure duct stripes are 10-15 mils thick and 3/16 to 3/8 inch wide.

rows.verbatim: The stripes shall be evenly spaced at 120° intervals around the circumference of the duct.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall space duct stripes evenly at 120-degree intervals around the duct circumference.

rows.verbatim: All conductors shall be copper or aluminum as indicated on the drawings.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use copper or aluminum conductors as indicated on the drawings.

rows.verbatim: Conductor shall be #10 AWG, XLP-USE insulation 0.045” thick.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide tracer conductor that is #10 AWG with XLP-USE insulation 0.045 inches thick.

rows.verbatim: Conductors shall be installed above conduits and tie wrapped to conduit.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall install tracer conductors above conduits and tie wrap them to the conduit.

rows.verbatim: Before any backfilling operations are begun, the Contractor and COR shall jointly inspect all trenches, cable placement, splice vaults, risers, marking tape, tracer conductors and other construction not accessible after backfilling.
rows.normalized: Contractor and COR must jointly inspect all trenches, cable placement, splice vaults, risers, marking tape, tracer conductors, and other construction not accessible after backfilling, before backfilling begins.

rows.verbatim: Trenching and backfill for electrical conduits shall conform to details shown in the drawings.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure trenching and backfill for electrical conduits conform to the drawings.

rows.verbatim: Coilable duct shall be directionally bored at standard burial depths of 36” of cover for ducts housing primary cables and 24” to 36” of cover for ducts housing secondary cables.
rows.normalized: Contractor must directionally bore coilable duct at specified burial depths for primary and secondary cable ducts.

rows.verbatim: Sections of coilable duct shall be joined using fusion couplings.
rows.normalized: Contractor must join sections of coilable duct using fusion couplings.

rows.verbatim: Prior to fusing, the Contractor shall make circumferential scores around the outside of the PVC conduit at the end that is to be installed into the fusion coupling.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make circumferential scores on the PVC conduit end prior to fusing it into the fusion coupling.

rows.verbatim: All vertical bends shall be made using Schedule 40 PVC bends with belled or coupled ends.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make all vertical bends using Schedule 40 PVC bends with belled or coupled ends.

rows.verbatim: Under no circumstances shall a vertical bend be fabricated by “sweeping” it up to grade using the guided boring machine.
rows.normalized: Contractor must never fabricate a vertical bend by sweeping it up to grade with the guided boring machine.

rows.verbatim: The vertical bend shall be joined directly to a 36” straight piece of matching size PVC conduit, which is installed to transition between the bend and the coilable duct.
rows.normalized: Contractor must join the vertical bend directly to a 36-inch straight matching-size PVC conduit piece as a transition to the coilable duct.

rows.verbatim: In places where the radius is too small for this, a PVC bend shall be installed between two 36” straight PVC transition sections.
rows.normalized: Where the radius is too small for sweeping, Contractor must install a PVC bend between two 36-inch straight PVC transition sections.

rows.verbatim: Bored coilable duct shall end 4’-5’ from a new vault or manhole.
rows.normalized: Contractor must end bored coilable duct 4 to 5 feet from a new vault or manhole.

rows.verbatim: This coilable duct shall then be transitioned to the same size PVC before connecting into the structure.
rows.normalized: Contractor must transition the coilable duct to same-size PVC before connecting into the structure.

rows.verbatim: The transition to PVC shall be made using the techniques described above in 3.3.B.2 – Duct Joining.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make the PVC transition using the techniques described in 3.3.B.2 Duct Joining.

rows.verbatim: Power, communications cable and fiber optic cable shall be installed in conduit only.
rows.normalized: Contractor must install power, communications, and fiber optic cable in conduit only.

rows.verbatim: Wherever possible, cable shall be played out from the reel mounted on a moving vehicle or trailer.
rows.normalized: Wherever possible, Contractor must play out cable from a reel mounted on a moving vehicle or trailer.

rows.verbatim:
Cable must be pulled through conduit; duct or other locations shall be lubricated with a
suitable cable lubricant approved by cable manufacturer prior to pulling into conduit or
duct.
rows.normalized: Contractor must pull cable through conduit and shall lubricate duct/other locations with a manufacturer-approved cable lubricant prior to pulling.

rows.verbatim: Bends will not be permitted within 12 inches of the ends of splice.
rows.normalized: Contractor will not be permitted to bend cable within 12 inches of splice ends.

rows.verbatim:
The cable or circuit numbers and the exact location of the splices shall be noted and given
to the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall note cable/circuit numbers and exact splice locations and give them to the COR.

rows.verbatim: Tracer conductor shall be tie wrapped with nylon straps to conduit every 10’.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall tie-wrap tracer conductor to conduit with nylon straps every 10 feet.

rows.verbatim: All exposed ends of conduit shall be plugged during construction.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall plug all exposed ends of conduit during construction.

rows.verbatim: No bends shall be permitted within six inches of the ends of stress cones.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall not permit bends within six inches of the ends of stress cones.

rows.verbatim: Grounding shall conform to Section 260010.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure grounding conforms to Section 260010.

rows.verbatim: The number of steps shall be from five to eight.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use five to eight steps when performing the stepped voltage test.

rows.verbatim: All faults discovered by this test shall be corrected and the tests rerun until cable splice meet requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall correct all faults discovered by the test and rerun the tests until the cable splice meets requirements.

rows.verbatim: The conductor shall be grounded to permit any charge to drain to earth.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ground the conductor to allow any charge to drain to earth.

rows.verbatim: Submit all test results in hard copy and PDF.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit all test results in hard copy and PDF.

rows.verbatim: Materials must be kept dry until ready to use.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep seed materials dry until ready to use.

rows.verbatim: Seeds shall be from Missouri eco-types or, if unavailable, from adjacent states.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use seeds from Missouri eco-types, or adjacent states if unavailable.

rows.verbatim: Seeding shall be at a rate recommended by the vendor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall seed at the rate recommended by the vendor.

rows.verbatim: In areas where slope is greater than 35%, then an annual rye and/or winter wheat and weed free straw shall be applied at 50 pounds per acre.
rows.normalized: If slope exceeds 35%, contractor shall apply annual rye and/or winter wheat and weed-free straw at 50 pounds per acre.

rows.verbatim: Topsoil shall have a pH range of 5.5 to 7.4.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide topsoil with a pH range of 5.5 to 7.4

rows.verbatim: NOTE: The C.O.R. shall approve the Contractor’s provided soil sample prior to installation and planting
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain C.O.R. approval of the provided soil sample before installation and planting begins

rows.verbatim: Spread organic topsoil at a minimum depth of 4 inches over area to be planted and integrate with the top layer of subsoil to prevent hardpan separation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must spread organic topsoil to a minimum depth of 4 inches over planting areas and integrate it with subsoil

rows.verbatim:
Seed shall be installed by means of mechanical and/or hand broadcast methods to ensure even
distribution of seeds throughout all designated seeded areas.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall install seed by mechanical and/or hand broadcast methods to ensure even distribution throughout all designated seeded areas.

rows.verbatim:
Native seed mix shall be mixed
thoroughly by vendor/supplier at their recommended ratios.
rows.normalized: Vendor/supplier shall thoroughly mix native seed mix at their recommended ratios.

rows.verbatim: Apply seed evenly in two intersecting directions.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall apply seed evenly in two intersecting directions.

rows.verbatim: Rake in lightly, then lightly mulch with clean, weed free straw.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall rake in lightly, then lightly mulch with clean, weed-free straw.

rows.verbatim:
Seeded areas shall be watered immediately following installation to accelerate
cover crop germination.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall water seeded areas immediately following installation to accelerate cover crop germination.

rows.verbatim: No bare spots larger than 1 square foot after substantial germination.
rows.normalized: Acceptable seed installation requires no bare spots larger than 1 square foot after substantial germination.

rows.verbatim: No more than 10% of the total area with bare spots larger than 1 square foot.
rows.normalized: Acceptable seed installation requires no more than 10% of total area with bare spots larger than 1 square foot.

rows.verbatim: A uniform coverage throughout all seeded areas.
rows.normalized: Acceptable seed installation requires uniform coverage throughout all seeded areas.

rows.verbatim: Do not perform seeding in windy conditions.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall not perform seeding in windy conditions.

rows.verbatim: Surface layer of soil for seeded areas shall be kept moist throughout gemination period.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall keep surface layer of soil for seeded areas moist throughout germination period.

rows.verbatim:
Mulch
the areas with a light covering of clean, chopped straw to retain moisture and use a tackifier to
prevent wind damage.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall mulch the areas with a light covering of clean, chopped straw to retain moisture and use a tackifier to prevent wind damage.

rows.verbatim:
If installed in spring, lightly water 4-6 weeks after germination at regular
intervals (depending on rainfall), or if an extended drought occurs throughout the summer months.
rows.normalized: If seed is installed in spring, contractor shall lightly water 4-6 weeks after germination at regular intervals, or if extended drought occurs during summer.

rows.verbatim:
Protect seeded areas from pedestrian traffic or vehicular trespassing with temporary fences, signs,
barriers, etc. while seed is germinating.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall protect seeded areas from pedestrian or vehicular trespassing with temporary fences, signs, barriers, etc. while seed is germinating.

rows.verbatim:
Repair damage resulting from trespass, erosion,
settlement, etc.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall repair damage resulting from trespass, erosion, settlement, etc.

rows.verbatim: Remove temporary protective devices after final acceptance.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall remove temporary protective devices after final acceptance.

rows.verbatim:
Maintain seeded areas immediately after placement until vegetation is well established and
exhibits a vigorous growing condition.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain seeded areas immediately after placement until vegetation is well established and exhibits vigorous growth.

rows.verbatim:
Control the growth of weeds to the extent possible by using various methods such as line
trimming, mowing and selective herbicide use.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall control weed growth to the extent possible using line trimming, mowing, and selective herbicide use.

rows.verbatim:
Apply herbicide in accordance with
manufacturer’s instructions.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall apply herbicide in accordance with manufacturer's instructions.

rows.verbatim: Contractor will be responsible for any damage resulting from improper use of herbicides.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for any damage resulting from improper use of herbicides.

rows.verbatim: Immediately reseed areas that show bare spots.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall immediately reseed areas that show bare spots.

rows.verbatim:
Well shall be pump tested to determine its maximum pumping rate at a stabilized drawdown which does not
exceed 1.5 times the design pumping rate (15 gpm) or the maximum amount the screen (if present) can
safely pass.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall pump test the well to determine maximum pumping rate at a stabilized drawdown not exceeding 1.5 times the design pumping rate (15 gpm) or the maximum the screen can safely pass.

rows.verbatim:
This reading should be the same as the original static
water level. If not, continue time and recordings until
the static water level has stabilized.
rows.normalized: If the 30-minute recovery reading does not match the original static water level, the person conducting the test shall continue timing and recording until the static water level stabilizes.

rows.verbatim:
Contractor to replace
existing control box to coordinate with new well pump.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall replace the existing control box to coordinate with the new well pump.

rows.verbatim:
Contractor to connect new electric to existing electric control
panel to power new well pump.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall connect new electric to the existing electric control panel to power the new well pump.
